name: Kerguelen Islands (French Southern Lands reserve)
blurb: Penguins, seals and albatrosses, plus rabbits and cats that reshaped the land.

tip.title: Remove the feral cats
tip.text: Set Feral cat to -100%. Rabbits lose a predator and rise, so Kerguelen cabbage, cushion plants and tussock are grazed harder, while king penguins lose a predator too.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Short, cool, often cloudy summers limit how much light reaches the plants and plankton that start the food web.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Microbes and soil invertebrates break down dead plants, carcasses and seabird waste, returning nutrients to the soil.
Drifting microscopic algae of the surrounding Southern Ocean, the base of the marine food web.
Introduced around 1874. It grazes cabbage, cushion plants and grasses, and is prey for feral cats and skuas.
Descended from ships cats. They hunt rabbits, mice and nesting seabirds, including penguins, on land.
Predator, pirate and scavenger: takes penguin chicks, eggs, seabirds, rabbits, fish and carrion.
Large petrel that kills penguin chicks and seabirds and scavenges carrion, notably from elephant seals.
Penguin of subantarctic coasts that feeds on fish and crustaceans such as krill, and is hunted by leopard seals and orcas.
Albatross that breeds at Kerguelen and eats fish, squid, crustaceans, carrion and fishery discards.
At Kerguelen it feeds mostly on fish and squid rather than krill, and its numbers there are growing.
Dives deep for squid and fish. Kerguelen holds about three-quarters of the Indian Ocean breeding population.
Predator of penguins and young seals, recorded killing weaned elephant seal pups.
Top marine predator that hunts penguins, seals and large whales.

story: The Kerguelen Islands are a group of islands in the subantarctic region within the French Southern and Antarctic Lands. The main island, Grande Terre, is 6,675 square kilometres in area. The islands are home to the Kerguelen cabbage and king penguins.
matters: The Kerguelen Islands shelter the king penguin, which breeds on subantarctic islands. Since the end of the whaling and sealing era, most of the islands' species have been able to increase their population again.
